knowledgePattern: Split an absolute-value curve before integrating its gap from a line

hints.title: Find where the formula changes
hints.body: Locate the zeros of x2−1 and the intersections with the horizontal line. Sketch which parts the modulus reflects.
hints.recap: An absolute-value curve changes formula where its inner expression changes sign.
hints.pitfall: Removing the modulus everywhere can change the enclosed region.
hints.pause: Mark the intersections and formula-change points.

recall.reminder: An absolute-value curve changes formula where its inner expression changes sign.

hints.title: Integrate the vertical gap
hints.body: Use upper curve minus lower curve on each resulting interval. Symmetry can shorten the calculation.
hints.recap: Total geometric area adds positive pieces; an integral without splitting may cancel them.
hints.pitfall: The horizontal line contributes a rectangle, not just its height.
hints.pause: Set up and evaluate the separate integrals.

recall.reminder: Total geometric area adds positive pieces; an integral without splitting may cancel them.

solution:
1. The intersections satisfy |x2−1|=3. The equation x2−1=−3 is impossible, while x2−1=3 gives x=±2. The line is above the curve between these intersections.

2. The curve is even. On 0≤x≤1, its height is 1−x2; on 1≤x≤2, it is x2−1.

3. The area is 2(∫01(2+x2)dx+∫12(4−x2)dx)=2(7/3+5/3)=8. Answer C.
